what: BPM Finder detects the tempo of a song, in beats per minute, from the audio file itself. Drop a file and it shows the BPM, the exact value, the length of one beat and how confident the result is.

It measures onsets (sudden rises in loudness in several frequency bands, like drum hits), tests every tempo from 55 to 215 BPM to see which beat grid lines up best, and fine-tunes the result with autocorrelation over many beats.
You can check the result by ear by playing the song with a click on every detected beat, switch to half or double time, or use Tap tempo for any song you hear. Everything runs in your browser.
uses: Find tempos to match songs or plan a set.
Pick songs that match your pace, such as 160 to 180 BPM for running.
Find songs for a dance style's tempo.
Set your project tempo to match a sample or reference track.
Know the tempo to set a metronome.
Cut clips on the beat by knowing the beat length in milliseconds.
tutorial: Click the box or drop an MP3, M4A, WAV, OGG or FLAC file. It needs at least 5 seconds of sound.
The big number is the tempo. Below it, the confidence shows High, Medium or Low with a percentage.
Press "Play with a click on each beat". If the clicks follow the music, the tempo is right.
If the number feels twice too fast or slow, press the half time or double time link.
The exact tempo, beat length in milliseconds and number of beats are shown underneath. Press Copy BPM to copy it.
For music playing elsewhere, tap the big button, the T key or the space bar on each beat. Four or more taps give a good average.
features: Shows how clear the beat is.
Hear clicks on the detected beats with the song.
Button, T key or space bar.

example.title: Worked example: matching songs for a run
example.text: Ama wants songs at about 170 steps a minute. She drops a song: BPM Finder shows 85 BPM with High confidence and suggests 170 as double time. She presses "Play with a click on each beat" and the clicks land on the kick drum, so she knows the song works at double time for running. For a song on the radio she taps along on the Tap button and gets 128 BPM.

tips: Songs with clear drums give the most confident results.
If confidence is Low, check by ear with the click, or use Tap tempo.
For DJ use, compare the exact value with decimals, not just the rounded number.
Tap tempo is most accurate after 8 or more taps; it restarts after a 2.5-second pause.
For long DJ mixes with tempo changes, analyse the songs one by one.
problems: It says no steady beat was found
The file may be speech, silence, a steady tone or very free music. Use Tap tempo instead.
The BPM is half or double what I expected
Both are valid ways to count. Press the half time or double time option.
The file could not be read
Your browser cannot decode this format. Convert it to MP3 with the Audio Converter.
The clicks drift away from the music
The song may change tempo or be played live without a click. The result is the average tempo.
